transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Newton Bridge CTO), Evelyn Park (Lead Engineer), Liam Ortiz (DevOps)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick round of intros. I'm Maya, AE on the account. Jordan is our SE.
[00:08] Samir Rao: Hi, Samir here, CTO at Newton Bridge. We build a smart reconciliation and customer support assistant for small banks.
[00:14] Evelyn Park: Evelyn, lead engineer, I'm focused on infra and the data pipeline.
[00:17] Liam Ortiz: Liam, DevOps, I handle network and compliance stuff.
[00:21] Jordan Patel: Hey all, Jordan, SE at Redwood, happy to dig into latency/cost tradeoffs.
[00:25] Maya Chen: Goal for this call: understand your immediate quickstart needs, confirm credits and TTFT expectations, and surface any blockers for hosted vs private.

Summary / Context
[00:40] Samir: We're in a prototyping phase. Want to spin up a small assistant that parses support tickets and reconciles transactions, we have some PII so privacy matters. Ideally get something running with minimal infra work — so self-serve API is attractive. But we need to know: how fast can we get to first token, what's included in credits, and what would push us to Dedicated or VPC?
[01:05] Maya: Perfect. TL;DR: for most teams TTFT is a day or less for a simple API integration — often minutes if you use our SDK/curl examples. Credits usually cover N tokens across text+embeddings; we'll grant a pilot credit bucket and a guide. If you see high sustained throughput or need isolated GPUs and strict egress controls, that's when Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) comes in.

Early technical questions
[01:32] Evelyn: Our data is sensitive. We need to understand retention, KMS, and audit logs. Do you expose keys or do we provision an HSM?
[01:40] Jordan: Right, so hosted flow: we encrypt data at rest, and for pilots we use our managed KMS; customers can request a dedicated KMS integration for Dedicated/Private tiers. We do retain logs for troubleshooting but you can opt for stricter retention policies. For SOC2 and enterprise needs, the Private option gives you full control over KMS and auditability.
[02:05] Liam: And network wise — if we do hosted, will outgoing traffic touch our VPC? We want to avoid data egress through unknown IPs.
[02:12] Maya: Hosted is over public egress, so if your compliance requires VPC peering or private connectivity we typically move you to Dedicated with Private connectivity or the Private product. We can also provide allow-listed IP ranges for hosted API egress to help with firewalling.

TTFT and credits specifics
[02:30] Samir: Walk me through a 'minute to first token' flow — what's needed on our side?
[02:36] Jordan: Minimal. Create an account, we send a trial API key + credits. You run a quick curl to /v1/generate with sample prompt or embeddings call. If you use our Node/Python SDK it wraps streaming and retries. For a naive PoC you can get a response in under five minutes; full integration with your app (auth, rate limits, tracing) usually a day or two.
[02:58] Evelyn: What does the credit bucket look like? Embeddings are more expensive for us.
[03:03] Maya: We usually give a starter package — for this pilot I'll propose $10k equivalent in hosted credits that can be used across endpoints. We'll also include a small dedicated benchmarking allowance (not full Dedicated cluster) so you can run a 1k-request latency and throughput test without being billed.
[03:22] Samir: Nice. Any limitations on model choice for trial?
[03:26] Jordan: You get access to our curated model catalog — default medium-latency models. If you want high-performance or quantized variants we can enable those but they may consume the credit bucket faster.

Performance and cost tradeoffs (real discussion)
[03:45] Liam: We're sensitive to tail latency. Our users are internal support agents so occasional 200–400ms variance is OK, but spikes above 1s are noticeable. What's Redwood's typical p50/p95 on hosted?
[03:58] Jordan: For hosted, for medium models we aim p50 ~120-250ms for generation token latency depending on prompt length; p95 can be 700-1,200ms under mixed traffic. If you need tighter p95 SLA, Dedicated with reserved capacity and tuned batching reduces variance significantly. We're transparent in the console about per-token breakdowns.
[04:20] Samir: How invasive is moving from hosted to Dedicated? We don't want a big rewrite.
[04:25] Maya: We designed the API to be consistent across environments. In most cases it's a config change and possibly new credentials. You can keep the same SDK codepaths; routing or hostnames change but API semantics stay the same.

Security/compliance specifics (friction points)
[04:40] Evelyn: For SOC2, do you have an attestation for hosted?
[04:43] Jordan: Redwood has SOC2 Type II for our platform. For certain customers we provide additional artifacts; for Private on-prem or VPC deployments you get more control and we support audit log forwarding.
[04:55] Evelyn: Data retention — can we disable model retention for pilot?
[04:58] Jordan: Yes, for pilots we can set a policy to not retain prompts/responses for model training; that's typical for PII workflows. We'll document it in the onboarding sheet.

Integration constraints & networking
[05:12] Liam: Our infra team wants a network diagram and an allowlist for IPs, also proxy header behavior.
[05:18] Jordan: We'll send the allowlist. For proxies we support standard TLS mutual TLS options on Private, and HTTP(S) with headers in hosted. Some header names might be normalized by proxies so we'll call that out.
[05:30] Maya: Liam, we'll include sample curl plus SDK samples — that usually helps unblock infra quickly.

Objections / cost sensitivity
[05:40] Samir: We're also watching costs — embeddings ingestion could blow through credits quickly. Any recommendations?
[05:45] Jordan: Two levers: reduce embedding dimensionality/use cheaper embedding models for bulk indexing; and batching/async embedding writes. Redwood Optimize also has suggestions — i.e., cache similar queries, incremental embeddings. We'll include quick tips in the onboarding doc.
[06:00] Evelyn: If we outgrow credits and see predictable load, what's the minimum for Dedicated?
[06:06] Maya: Minimum reserved commitments vary; typically teams move to Dedicated when sustained qps exceeds a few hundred requests per minute for latency-sensitive production. We can draft a ramp plan tied to your cost thresholds.

Concrete next steps recap (end of call)
[06:25] Maya: To recap: Redwood will grant a $10k pilot credit, send an onboarding checklist and allowlist, Jordan will share a 1k-req benchmark script and sample SDK calls, and Newton Bridge will confirm compliance scope and provide a network diagram. We'll schedule a 30min tech deep dive the week of Dec 20.
[06:48] Samir: Sounds good. I also want a rough cost estimate for embeddings at 100k vectors/month so we can plan.
[06:53] Jordan: We'll include a back-of-envelope cost with the benchmarking results.

Wrap & informal notes
[07:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll send follow ups shortly.
[07:03] Evelyn: Appreciate it.
[07:04] Liam: Thanks all.

(Transcript ends — occasional misrecognitions: "allowlist" sometimes rendered as "all-list", "KMS" as "K M S", and some punctuation missing.)
